summary: Idle-based agent timeout replacing absolute wall-clock deadline so active agents are not killed while producing output, and user git identity attribution with Bored co-author trailer on all agent commits.

items: Idle-based agent timeout — timeout now resets on every line of stdout/stderr output instead of using an absolute wall-clock deadline, so active agents producing logs, tool calls, or streaming responses are no longer killed while making progress; timeout only fires when the process goes silent for the configured duration
Shared last_activity tracker updated by stream reader threads on each line read, with per-attempt fresh idle timers replacing the global deadline logic

User git identity attribution — agent commits now show the user as author/committer by injecting GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* env vars read from the repo's git config chain (repo → global → system), matching the pattern used by GitHub Copilot and Claude Code
Bored co-author trailer — add-and-commit instructions require a "Co-authored-by: Bored <agent@bored.local>" trailer on every agent commit so Bored is credited as co-author
Initial commits in new repos no longer pollute repo-level git config — switched from git config user.name/user.email writes to per-invocation env vars for author/committer identity
